newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's ANC to meet Inkatha on constitution.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ANC to meet Inkatha on constitution.

text.p: South Africa's ruling African National Congress (ANC) will hold talks with its rival Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) on Wednesday on amending disputed portions of the new constitution, a spokesman said on Tuesday.
ANC Secretary-General Cyril Ramaphosa is slated to head the delegation, which would include Constitutional Development Minister Mohammed Valli Moosa, ANC spokesman Ronnie Mamoepa told reporters.
"The meeting follows a request by the IFP national council last weekend to hold a meeting with the ANC to discuss constitutional issues," he said.
"The ANC has committed itself to a process of bilateral and multilateral meetings with all other political parties, including the IFP, involving the constitution-making process."
Mamoepa declined to elaborate and no comment was immediately available from Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi's Inkatha.
Inkatha, main black rival of the ANC, walked out of the constitution-making process 18 months ago in protest over the ANC's refusal to allow international mediation on their differences.
Inkatha demands strong autonomy for provincial governments but the ANC wants most power to be wielded by the central government.

The Constitutional Court this month rejected parts of the new constitution approved by parliament in May and sent them back for redrafting including those dealing with the powers of provinces, the main point of contention between Inkatha and the ANC.

Buthelezi said on Sunday that in light of the court's decision Inkatha would meet the ANC to discuss the necessary amendments. But he stopped short of saying his party would participate in redrafting the constitution.
The Zulu-based Inkatha has majority support in KwaZulu-Natal province. An estimated 15,000 people have been killed there in a decade of feuding between Inkatha and the ANC.

A new version of the constitution must be submitted to the Constitutional Court by October 11 if it is to come into force in January, replacing an interim constitution that was adopted during the last days of the old apartheid government.
ANC leaders have said they are unwilling to let the IFP reopen negotiations over all aspects of the document. The Constitutional Court said it expected only minor adjustments.
Mamoepa said the talks with Inkatha would begin at 8 a.m. (0600 GMT) in Cape Town.
